key_insight: Quasi-SVD replaces fully sequential SVD with a Lie-constrained, fully parallel GPU factorisation to make matrix decomposition fast enough for real-time imaging.
clinical_relevance: It could enable live processing in image-guided workflows such as ultrasound localisation microscopy and tissue polarimetry, where current SVD methods are too slow for clinical throughput.
method: Uses a differentiable, fully parallel matrix factorisation on GPUs
Enforces exact orthogonality on one Lie-parameterized factor and soft constraints on the rest
Prioritises reconstruction fidelity over exact spectral recovery
evidence_signal: Across two medical imaging tasks and multiple instruments, the method reported SSIM 0.89-0.94, 3-20x speedups over cuSOLVER/randomised SVD, and throughput above 25 FPS.
watch_item: The approach trades exact singular-vector recovery for speed, so clinical deployment would still need validation that the approximation is reliable across new scanners, matrices, and edge cases.
paper_title: Quasi-SVD: Learning a Lie-constrained matrix factorisation for real-time imaging
